title: Obtain a release-sized Middle Persian transcription for the Herrmann audit
statement: I checked the corpus dependency for Herrmann's 2017 Pahlavi claim. In the CC BY 4.0 Multimedia Yasna edition, I counted text in elements explicitly tagged xml:lang=pal-Phlv, omitting gaps, in the eight published XML sets each for Pt4 (AV_400) and J2 (AV_500). Normalization using the reference corpus cleaner gave 61,561 and 45,433 characters respectively. Those are witnesses of overlapping material. Coverage and license at https://muya.soas.ac.uk/tool/transcriptions-editions/ and https://transcriptions.soas.ac.uk/edition/home/index.xml. In the 2026-06-01 CC BY 4.0 Invisible East JSON release https://zenodo.org/records/20490171 I found 158 records with primary language Middle Persian (Pahlavi script), and 16 folios with populated transcription fields. Removing markup and normalizing gave 1,768 transcription characters. OpenAMPD's catalogue footer specifies CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 at https://mp.melc.berkeley.edu/exist/apps/OpenAMPD/index.html. The public-domain 1868 Justi scan has machine OCR, with visibly garbled copy on the original-script pages and with German text also present in the OCR stream (https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_Pg4ZHN574VYC). MPCD has ample source material. Rahnamoun and Rahnamoun 2025, Table 1, reports 36,894 tokens for the Greater Bundahishn from MPCD (https://aclanthology.org/2025.clrel-1.3/). The UD MPCD repository declares CC BY-SA 4.0, and at dev commit e23e1918891c1991a2851d7ac3460e7b7909530a it contains documentation and a licence without a text dataset (https://github.com/UniversalDependencies/UD_Middle_Persian-MPCD/tree/e23e1918891c1991a2851d7ac3460e7b7909530a). I could not verify a qualifying plain-text release at the scorer's 150,000-character threshold. No corpus or attack verdict follows from these checks.
check: Use a versioned, licensed MPCD or UD release with actual text. Export a single witness per work and separate phonographic Middle Persian from diplomatic transliteration, editions' apparatus and translations. Record the licence, normalization, byte hash and clean character count before submitting a corpus experiment. For the later Herrmann audit, specify how proposed word-separator and abbreviation signs in section 2 and Table 1 are represented before running any decoys.
